ai.title: Drop invalid Freebuff login auth codes
ai.summary: Invalid CLI auth codes are now rejected during login, preventing malformed or opaque tokens from being forwarded to the `/onboard` route. A new `cli-auth-code-shape.ts` module centralizes regex validation and parsing logic, replacing inline checks in `_helpers.ts`. The change affects Web UI login flows (`/login`, `sign-in-button`, `login-card`) and NextAuth redirect handling (`auth-options.ts`). `getCliAuthOnboardSearchParams` explicitly strips invalid `auth_code` parameters before redirecting, ensuring only valid codes persist in the URL.

eli5.text: If you try to log in with a login code that doesn't match the expected format, the system will now refuse to accept it instead of passing it along to the next step. This affects anyone using the web login flow, especially when coming in from a command-line tool. The code that checks these login codes has been moved into one shared place so it's easier to maintain, and the login buttons and redirect logic now use that single set of rules. You would notice this when attempting to sign in with a malformed or tampered login token: instead of seeing a confusing error later, the invalid code is rejected up front.

ai.title: extractApiErrorDetails unwraps nested AI SDK retry errors
ai.summary: New `extractApiErrorDetails` in `common/src/util/error.ts` traverses `lastError`, `errors`, and `cause` chains to pull status codes and parsed response bodies from nested AI SDK `RetryError` wrappers. Replaces direct `parseApiErrorResponseBody` calls in `sdk/src/run.ts` and `packages/agent-runtime/src/run-agent-step.ts`, ensuring accurate error reporting when upstream failures are wrapped. Docs updated in `docs/error-schema.md` to reflect the new `session_superseded` 409 error code.

eli5.text: When something goes wrong during an AI-powered coding session, you now get a clearer message about what happened and why. The system can now dig through layers of wrapped errors from the AI provider to pull out the real status code and message, so failures that were previously reported as generic or confusing now show their true cause. If you've ever seen a vague failure when the AI service hit an issue behind the scenes, that message should now explain the actual problem, like a rate limit or authentication issue, instead of hiding it.

ai.title: Remove padded count from limited landing session counter
ai.summary: The waiting-room screen's session counter now uses `formatSessionUnits` instead of `formattedSharedPremiumUsed` to display the used count. This drops zero-padding from the number. Scope limited to `cli/src/components/waiting-room-screen.tsx`.

eli5.text: The waiting-room screen's session counter now displays the used count without zero-padding, so a number like '007' appears as '7'. This affects anyone who sees the session counter while in the waiting room, making the displayed number slightly shorter. If you looked at the screen before and after, you'd notice the 'used' count no longer has leading zeros.

ai.title: Freebuff bumps to 0.0.89 packaging live usage dashboard and DeepSeek
ai.summary: Bumped the Freebuff release package version from 0.0.88 to 0.0.89 in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json`. This release rolls up the same-day user-visible features: a `/live` usage dashboard, analytics sampling with `CODEBUFF_FULL_TELEMETRY` env vars, local token counting for DeepSeek Flash, a new limited DeepSeek access tier, premium reset countdowns, and invalid Freebuff login auth-code rejection. Database migration 0052 and the `FREEBUFF_DEV_FORCE_LIMITED` dev env var also ship with this packaging commit, affecting CLI, Web, and shared Core surfaces.
ai.evidence: The file `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` was modified, changing the `version` field from `0.0.88` to `0.0.89` as a release-bump commit with +1/-1 line changes.

eli5.text: This release adds a new live usage dashboard so you can see Freebuff activity by country and AI model in real time, introduces DeepSeek as a limited-option AI model in the CLI model selector, and adds tiered access controls that distinguish limited sessions from premium sessions. A countdown now shows how long until your free premium quota resets each day, and the waiting-room screen displays the next reset time using local timezone logic. Free-mode traffic now skips heavy billing writes and caches country-access decisions, while analytics sampling reduces telemetry load by default unless full debugging is enabled. CLI ad requests now include a user-agent header so ad networks correctly identify terminal-based traffic, and invalid login auth codes are rejected and logged with detailed metadata to help diagnose authentication failures. Error reporting now unwraps nested AI SDK retry failures for more accurate messages, and the limited-mode landing screen uses a simplified confirm-gate panel with better-readable button text.

ai.title: Freebuff CLI version bumped to 1.0.676
ai.summary: The CLI release package manifest in `cli/release/package.json` was updated to version 1.0.676, incrementing from 1.0.675. This is a release-bump commit that packages the preceding day's user-visible changes for distribution. The increment rolls up notable features from 2026-05-13 including ZeroClick ad display text fixes, a live usage dashboard, analytics sampling, limited DeepSeek access, and nested AI SDK error unwrapping.
ai.evidence: The diff for `cli/release/package.json` shows the `version` field changed from `1.0.675` to `1.0.676`, a single-line version bump in the release manifest.

eli5.text: Freebuff CLI 1.0.676 ships a new live usage dashboard, improved Freebuff premium session reset countdown, and limited access tier support for DeepSeek. A new /live page shows real-time usage maps by country and model; the waiting room now displays a clear countdown to your next quota reset; and limited-tier users see a simplified landing screen instead of the full model picker. Security gets tighter auth-code validation, rejection of malformed login tokens, and detailed debug logging for failed CLI logins. Analytics now sample high-volume events at 1% by default to reduce load, and ad requests sent from the CLI now carry a proper User-Agent header so ad networks target correctly. Behind the scenes, caching country access decisions, skipping remote token counting for free DeepSeek agents, and bypassing credit ledger writes for free-mode requests all combine to make free-tier usage faster and smoother.

ai.title: Fix model switch landing
ai.summary: Fix freebuff model switch landing (#669) by preserving metadata during session transitions. `use-freebuff-session.ts` introduces `toLandingSession` to extract `accessTier`, `queueDepthByModel`, and `rateLimitsByModel` from the current state before resetting status to 'none'. `session-ended-banner.tsx` updates button labels to 'Back to start' for limited tiers and 'Change model' otherwise, using dynamic pending states. Scope: CLI session hooks and UI components. Detail: `apply({ status: 'none' })` replaced with `apply(landingSession)` to prevent metadata loss on rejoin or return-to-landing.

eli5.text: When you use the CLI to switch models or return to the start screen, your session's access tier, queue depth, and rate limits were being thrown away, causing the screen to forget important details about your tier. Now the landing logic preserves that metadata so limited-tier users see 'Back to start' and others see 'Change model', with matching loading labels. This affects CLI users switching models or returning to the landing screen in Freebuff sessions, and the fix is live as part of release 1.0.676.

ai.title: CLI waiting room labels limited access reason
ai.summary: Waiting room screen now displays specific limited access reasons like 'hosting network detected' or 'outside available countries' instead of generic text. Server responses (session-view, handlers) and common types now propagate countryCode, countryBlockReason, and ipPrivacySignals to the client. Covers CLI, Shared/Core, and Web surfaces.

eli5.text: When you land on the waiting-room screen in the CLI app, you'll now see a specific reason for why you're seeing a reduced set of models instead of a generic message. For example, you might see 'hosting network detected' or 'outside available countries (FR),' which tells you exactly why your access is limited. The server now sends your country code, the specific reason your IP was blocked, and any privacy-related signals (like VPN or Tor usage) directly to the client, so the app doesn't have to figure it out locally.

ai.title: Freebuff version bumped to 0.0.90
ai.summary: The Freebuff release package version increased from 0.0.89 to 0.0.90 in freebuff/cli/release/package.json. This release-bump commit captures the 0.0.90 release, which includes the user-visible model switch landing fix (preserving accessTier, queueDepthByModel, and rateLimitsByModel during session transitions), specific limited access waiting-room reasons (hosting network, country restrictions), and the Freebuff 1.0.676 model picker reordering and /live dashboard bundle detailed in the surrounding same-day commit sequence.
ai.evidence: Modified file: freebuff/cli/release/package.json, the version field changed from "0.0.89" to "0.0.90" in the diff hunk, with no other changes to the file.

eli5.text: This release makes model switching smoother and waiting-room messaging clearer for users. When you switch between AI models during a session, important information like your access level, queue depth, and rate limits is now preserved instead of being lost, so reconnects and returns to the landing screen behave correctly. The waiting room screen now shows specific, plain-language reasons for limited access, such as 'hosting network detected' or 'outside available countries', instead of generic text. Your buttons will also adjust dynamically, showing 'Back to start' for limited tiers and 'Change model' for others, with proper pending states while loading. Upgrading means fewer surprises when switching models or hitting capacity limits, and you'll always understand why access is restricted when it happens.

ai.title: Overhaul Freebuff live map
ai.summary: Live map now uses accurate Natural Earth geometry and Equal Earth projection instead of hand-drawn blobs. Country centroids moved to generated `world-map-data.ts` via REST Countries data. `live-client.tsx` applies proper projection math for rendering. Covers Web `/live` surface.

eli5.text: When you open the live map on the website, you now see properly shaped countries drawn from real geographic data instead of rough hand-drawn outlines. Each country marker is placed at its true center point, pulled from an official country database, and the whole map uses a balanced projection that keeps landmasses looking correctly sized. You can tell because coastlines, borders, and marker positions look accurate rather than sketchy.
